entities.summary:
René de Froulay, Count of Tessé was a nobleman from Le Mans, who served Louis XIV of France as a soldier and diplomat.

Born in 1648, René de Froulay was the son of Jacques de Froulay and Claude de Tressan. He married Françoise de La Roche, and together they had several children.

In 1667, René de Froulay was appointed as the governor of the province of Normandy, a position he held until his death in 1725.

During his tenure, he implemented various reforms to improve the lives of the peasants and promoted trade and commerce in the region.

René de Froulay was also known for his military prowess, having fought in several battles against the English and the Dutch.

He died on March 30, 1725, at the age of 76, leaving behind a legacy of service to his country and his people.

As he once said, 'A true leader is not one who seeks power, but one who serves others.'
